# The first-steps walkthrough

The product ships a runnable example workflow. Copy it, run one verb against a
deployment, and watch the instance to completion.

## The shipped example

```yaml
name: onboarding
version: "1"
description: |
  First-steps walkthrough template.
nodes:
  - type: verifier
    executor: verifier-shape-checks
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          checks:
            type: array
            default:
              - kind: no_nulls
                config:
                  field: id
              - kind: pk_unique
                config:
                  field: id
          rows:
            type: array
            default:
              - id: alpha
                value: 1
              - id: beta
                value: 2
              - id: gamma
                value: 3
        required: [checks, rows]
```

The defaults bake the inputs into the template, so the run needs no params. The
node references the bundled `verifier-shape-checks` executor and runs real
verification work — `no_nulls` and `pk_unique` against three rows.

The deployment must declare the `verifier-shape-checks` executor. Without it the
executor reference fails at template-deploy time.

## Run it

```bash
rimsky run --endpoint "$BASE" --instance-key onboarding-1 ./onboarding-template.yaml
```

The verb registers the template, deploys it, creates an instance, and prints:

```
instance_id=<uuid>
```

It exits 0.

## Watch it

```bash
rimsky watch --endpoint "$BASE" --poll-interval 250ms "$INSTANCE_ID"
```

`watch` returns 0 once the instance reaches a terminal state.

```bash
rimsky instance status "$INSTANCE_ID" --endpoint "$BASE" -o json
# terminal/success
```

## The two verbs as a script

The shipped walkthrough script wraps the same two verbs:

```bash
RIMSKY_BIN=rimsky RIMSKY_CONTROL_API_URL="$BASE" bash ./onboarding-demo.sh
```

It runs end to end and prints its completion line:

```
onboarding-demo: instance <uuid> reached terminal — dev-loop walkthrough complete
```

Both the template and the script run unedited from a copy, so nothing depends on
staying inside the project tree.
